key_insight: The paper argues that safe AI in healthcare needs "alignment plausibility": a three-part demonstration that values, training, and oversight all support positive patient outcomes.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare systems using LLMs in mental health support, this framework shifts safety assessment from reacting to obvious harms to proving ongoing, clinically grounded risk control.
method: Define explicit values from established clinical norms and duties.
Embed those values through training and model development.
Use deployment oversight to detect drift, dependency, boundary erosion, and other longer-term harms.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a conceptual proposal rather than an empirical study, so it does not present new patient data or outcome evaluation.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is operationalizing "positive health outcomes" and monitoring subtle harms consistently across real-world deployments.
paper_title: Alignment Plausibility: A New Standard for Assuring AI in Healthcare
